# Codebook

Unit: one row per firm (2000 software and engineering firms). Cross-section.

| column | description |
|---|---|
| firm_id | Firm identifier |
| remote_share | Share of engineering staff working mostly remote, 2021-2022 |
| patents_per_100_eng_2023 | Patent applications per 100 engineers in 2023 |
| log_engineers_2020 | Log number of engineers, 2020 |
| firm_age_2020 | Firm age in years, standardized, 2020 |
| patents_per_100_eng_2020 | Patent applications per 100 engineers in 2020, standardized |
| collab_index_2023 | Internal collaboration index from 2023 survey |
| region | Region (north, central, south) |
| listed | 1 if publicly listed |
| segment | Sector: hardware / software |
| vc_backed | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| founder_ceo | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| cloud_spend_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| hq_in_hub_city | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| share_phd_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| gross_margin_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
# Report

Question: What is the effect of remote work on engineering innovation?

Approach: OLS of patents_per_100_eng_2023 on remote_share with heteroskedasticity-robust (HC1) standard errors. I control for firm size and firm age and trim the top and bottom 1% of the outcome.

Result: the coefficient on remote_share is 0.730 (SE 0.222, p = 0.0010, N = 1960).

Conclusion: positive effect.

Specifications estimated: 1 (the one above). Code: analysis.py.

d=pd.read_csv('data.csv')

for f in ['patents_per_100_eng_2023 ~ remote_share','patents_per_100_eng_2023 ~ remote_share+log_engineers_2020+firm_age_2020',
'patents_per_100_eng_2023 ~ remote_share+log_engineers_2020+firm_age_2020+patents_per_100_eng_2020',
'patents_per_100_eng_2023 ~ remote_share+log_engineers_2020+firm_age_2020+patents_per_100_eng_2020+vc_backed+founder_ceo+cloud_spend_2020+hq_in_hub_city+share_phd_2020+gross_margin_2020+C(region)+listed+C(segment)']:
    m=smf.ols(f,d).fit(cov_type='HC1');print(m.params['remote_share'],m.bse['remote_share'],m.pvalues['remote_share'])
print(d.corr(numeric_only=True)['remote_share'])

import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm

df = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
y = df["patents_per_100_eng_2023"]
lo, hi = y.quantile([0.01, 0.99])
df = df[(y >= lo) & (y <= hi)]
X = sm.add_constant(df[['remote_share', 'log_engineers_2020', 'firm_age_2020']].astype(float))
fit = sm.OLS(df["patents_per_100_eng_2023"].values, X.values).fit(cov_type="HC1")
print("n =", len(df))
print("coef =", fit.params[1], "se =", fit.bse[1], "p =", fit.pvalues[1])

content.text:
I approved the report and wrote `verdict.json`.

I re-ran the regression of 2023 patents per 100 engineers on `remote_share`. The effect stayed positive and significant under each control set I tried:

| Controls | Coefficient on `remote_share` | p-value |
|---|---|---|
| None | 2.32 | about 1e-21 |
| Firm size and age | 0.83 | 0.0004 |
| Size, age and the 2020 patent rate | 0.75 | 0.001 |
| All pre-period controls, plus region, segment and listed status | 0.75 | 0.001 |

The analyst's own estimate of 0.73 sits in line with these. Their code also matches what the report describes, with one specification and a 1% trim of the outcome.

The report doesn't control for `collab_index_2023`. That index is measured after the remote shift, so it is a mediator, and leaving it out is correct. The effect is modest: about 0.75 patents per 100 engineers per standardised unit of remote share, on an outcome averaging about 100.

Two limits I did not test further. The data are a single cross-section, so the causal reading rests on the controls. I also did not check whether the effect differs across subgroups.
